title: Collapsed Effective Operators for Higher-order Structures
claim: Collapsing higher-order structure into a vertex-level operator yields modes that follow meaningful structural units, unlike modes from the plain graph Laplacian.
layout: 5 panels in a row, left-to-right, Roman numeral labels, no arrows
description: A single horizontal strip of five renderings of the same protein (1A0C), labeled I–V underneath. Panel I is a ribbon diagram showing helices and strands in varied colors. Panel II is a sphere cloud of residues colored by a smooth rainbow-like gradient along the backbone, from red at the top through green to purple at the tail, showing the graph-Laplacian modes. Panel III shows the same spheres recolored by the collapsed operator. It has sharper, patchier color regions that match secondary-structure elements, such as pink, bright green, blue and olive. Panel IV is an orange backbone trace with a grey graph overlay. Panel V shows the collapsed operator as red helix slabs, blue sheet slabs and grey coupling lines over the orange backbone. The eye goes first to the colorful sphere panels II and III.
caption: Our Collapsed effective operators reveal secondary-structure-aware spectral modes. On protein 1A0C (437 residues) from Topotein (Wang et al., 2025), we color residues by the leading spectral embedding (top-3 joint-PCA components of the leading eigenvectors) of our collapsed operator S versus the graph Laplacian L𝐺, aligned so matching modes share colors. Left to right: (I) the secondary structure, shown as helical ribbons and 𝛽-strand arrows; (II) L𝐺produces smoother, backbone-sequential modes; (III) modes from S are organized around secondary-structure elements (SSEs); (IV) the backbone graph underlying L𝐺; and (V) S as a vertex-level operator, with SSE cells collapsed into within-cell couplings on the backbone and colored by class (helix red, sheet blue, coil grey).
abstract: Higher-order structures are powerful relational modeling tools, yet existing spectral operators decompose the topology into separate ranks, leaving practitioners to fuse the information back to vertices through ad hoc choices. We introduce Collapsed Effective Operators, which condense higher-order degrees of freedom into a single vertex-level operator via Schur complementation of a graded Laplacian. This yields a (generally dense) operator that encodes long-range interactions mediated by topology and is applicable to arbitrary higher-order constructs. We show it preserves positive semi-definiteness with a spectral upper bound relative to the rank-0 Hodge Laplacian, effectively lowering system energy under higher-order connectivity. Empirically, our operator improves spectral clustering, signal smoothing, and enables the inclusion of topological features in neural network architectures via positional encoding. The project page can be found http://circle-group.github.io/research/CollapsedEffectiveOperators
